Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T48/T48n2001.xml). Extensive Record of Chan Master Hongzhi. Hongzhi Zhengjue owns the retained address: before the trace of blue and white, beyond parting and subtlety — sit astride the heads of the retribution and transformation buddhas, see no phase of forming, abiding, breaking; therefore it is said: lay the whole body down, and only then do you first understand undertaking — and what is the affair of undertaking? a long silence: spring spent in the ten isles, flowers withering; in the coral grove the sun shines bright.

Occurrences.Kwic: 今多少靈利人。向一色邊立定主宰。一切處禪將去。禪也禪得是。儞若不親向自己脚根下卒地斷嚗地折一回。殊不知和箇禪底。亦不曾脫他輪回生死。此事是博地凡夫。立地便要向他佛祖頭上坐臥。要於一剎那頃將他積刦根深蔕固底輪回生死連底一󷘓󷘓轉。是謂大事因緣。豈口出耳入而能及之者哉。如果未相應。且不要人別求方便。但只於十二時全身放下。單單靠取箇所叅話頭。日亦然夜亦然。行亦然坐亦然。生亦然死亦然。乃至上刀山入劒林亦皆然。更不生第二念。只麼純一無雜挨拶將去。久久純熟和箇亦然底同時脫略。心空及第其在斯焉。政與麼時喚一陽作六隂也得。喚六隂作一陽也得。喚全消是長亦得。喚全長是消亦得。喚不消不長即消即長總得。可謂真正衲子本色道流。遇緣即宗應時納
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (B/B25/B25n0145.xml). Extensive Record of Zhongfeng Mingben of Tianmu. Zhongfeng Mingben owns the retained instruction: seek no other expedient — through the twelve hours lay the whole body down, lean singly on the examined saying: so by day, so by night; walking, sitting; living, dying; up the knife-mountain, into the sword-forest — no second thought rising; push through pure and unmixed, and when long ripened, even the 'so-it-is' drops off together — the empty-mind graduation falls just here.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X71/X71n1409.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yuejiang Zhengyin. Yuejiang Zhengyin owns the retained instruction: brothers — unless you truly mean to settle the great affair of birth and death, stake ten years, twenty years of work: lay the whole body down, lean on a true-rooted workman and have it out with him — like gold in the ore entering the furnace and bellows, taking the tongs and hammer, smelted a thousand times till the dross is gone and the gold's own body stands forth of itself; and that gold is your own originally-held body, never borrowed from outside.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X63/X63n1257.xml). Boshan's Chan Admonitions. Wuyi Yuanlai owns the retained admonition: when the doubt-spring will not rise, do not go counting lines and inking letters, threading the buddhas' and founders' words into one stamp — that is the rising-and-falling mind, not Chan; but if you will know the wrong in a single thought, lay the whole body down, see a knowing friend and ask him for a way in — that will do; else the rising-and-falling mind wins, and in time it becomes a haunting no remedy reaches.

Hanxiu Ruqian owns the retained exhortation: failing that, then just here, under three rafters and before the seven-foot mat — hang the alms-bag high, lay the whole body down, rear the raw-iron spine and spine through, set a date and take the proof: all at once a bean bursts in the cold ash and the face-gate splits — and the end never leaves this spot.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (L/L155/L155n1643.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hongjue Min. Muchen Daomin owns the retained verdict: if it is truly so — the whole body laid down, the chasing-seeking rested — then the site never stirred though you walked all hundred cities, the tower-gates stay shut though you circled the whole realm: your seeking is finished, the mountain monk's work in the world is done; and the address closes on the seal he was ordered not to hand around carelessly.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB407.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shengren of Qianshan. Qianshan Shengren Hanke owns the retained stake: the three-age buddhas cannot lift it, the founders cannot hand it on — a true great man lays the whole body down before the yellow-faced elder ever left home, before the blue-eyed one ever came west, and then he can charge crosswise and fling aslant: cold, riding the stone horse, win back the desert wind; by night, loose the mud ox to tread the bright moon of the clear pool to pieces.

Senses.Explanation: Lay the whole body down: the precondition of undertaking, the twelve-hour stake, the raw-iron spine upright under three rafters — everything held, set down entire. Hongzhi Zhengjue, in the hall: sit astride the heads of the retribution and transformation buddhas, see no phase of forming, abiding, breaking — therefore it is said: lay the whole body down, and only then do you first understand undertaking; and what is the affair of undertaking? a long silence — spring spent in the ten isles, flowers withering; in the coral grove the sun shines bright. Zhongfeng Mingben, instructing the trainee: seek no other expedient — through the twelve hours lay the whole body down, lean singly on the examined saying; so by day, so by night; walking, sitting; living, dying; up the knife-mountain, into the sword-forest; no second thought rising — push through pure and unmixed, and when long ripened even the 'so-it-is' drops off together: the empty-mind graduation falls just here. Yuejiang Zhengyin, to the brothers: unless you truly mean to settle the great affair, stake ten years, twenty years: lay the whole body down, lean on a true-rooted workman and have it out — gold in the ore, furnace and bellows, tongs and hammer, smelted a thousand times till the dross is gone and the gold's own body stands forth; and it never was borrowed from outside. Wuyi Yuanlai, in the Admonitions: when the doubt-spring will not rise, do not go threading the words into one stamp — that is the rising-and-falling mind; but know the wrong in a single thought, lay the whole body down, see a knowing friend and ask for a way in. Hanxiu Ruqian, opening the retreat: if not that, then just here, under three rafters before the seven-foot mat, hang the alms-bag high, lay the whole body down, rear the raw-iron spine, set a date and take the proof — all at once a bean bursts in the cold ash, the face-gate splits, and the end never leaves this spot. Muchen Daomin, in the hall: if it is truly so — the whole body laid down, the chasing-seeking rested — the site never stirred though you walked all hundred cities, the tower-gates stay shut though you circled the realm: your seeking is finished, the mountain monk's work in the world is done. Qianshan Shengren Hanke, before the assembly: the three-age buddhas cannot lift it, the founders cannot hand it on; a true great man lays the whole body down before the yellow-faced elder left home and before the blue-eyed one came west — then he can charge crosswise and fling aslant: cold, riding the stone horse, win back the desert wind; by night, loose the mud ox to tread the bright moon of the clear pool to pieces.
